Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:73: The fourth Heichal is called Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay], and corresponding to it, the evil inclination is called "stumbling-stone." This Heichal is called Chovah [Debt/Guilt] because it corresponds to the Heichal of Merit; and all the debts and sins of people - there are in this Heichal several angels of destruction who gather them and bring them into this Heichal. And on the Day of Judgment, when merit and guilt are weighed, if the scale of merit, the side of holiness, tips, it is holy and they are judged for life; and if the scale of guilt tips, several creditors seize it and say, it is ours, and rejoice in it, and judge him to death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:74: Come and see: just as a person conducts himself in this world, so is drawn and poured upon him from above. If he pursues the impure side and transgressions, the spirit of impurity pursues him and helps him become more impure, and causes him to come to graver transgressions and impurities more crushing than the first. But if a person purifies himself and pursues holiness and sanctifies himself, a spirit of holiness is drawn and poured upon him and purifies him and sanctifies him and clothes him in humility and fear and brings him to greater purity - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in tractate Avodah Zarah, first chapter: watchfulness leads to alacrity, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:75: In this Heichal is the place of all those called "other gods" - these are the ones who entice people with the pleasures of this world, with adulteries and lewdness; and over all these called "other gods" there is a spirit that rules over all of them, called El Nechar [Foreign God], and he entices those who study Torah, standing in the study hall, with evil thoughts and filth, and says to them: why do you stand here, wasting your youth in the occupation of study and weakening your strength? Is it not better for you to rejoice in your youth with adulteries and lewdness? And when a person is enticed after him, several masters of impurity follow after him to defile him in this world, and all these are called "boiling excrement," standing to defile a person, as I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:76: In the middle of this Heichal there is one spirit named Nega [Plague], and from him another spirit spreads out, called Nega Tzara'at [Plague of Leprosy], and they stand to defile all those masters of evil speech more than all the others who defile. The upper Nega we mentioned is appointed to curse all those tables that were not arranged properly for the Sabbath - they are all arrayed before him and he curses them with intense curses that need not be elaborated - may the Merciful One save us; as is the way of holiness for good, so is the way of impurity for evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:77: In this Heichal hang, for evil, all matters except for children, life, and sustenance, which hang above in the other Heichalot and descend to this Heichal, and from there emerge to prosecute for evil - whether to diminish people, to kill them, or to diminish their sustenance - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:78: From this Heichal goes forth one impure spirit named Arira, and under his hand several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction, and they are all called "cursers of the day"; and they are appointed over one who curses himself in anger, or over that oath of imprecation and curse, and they bring it up above and arouse with it the primordial serpent, the Leviathan, the twisting serpent, that he may rise and arouse intense curses, Heaven forfend. And this is what Job intended when he said (Job 3:8), "let those who curse the day curse it" - these are the ones destined to arouse Leviathan, who is the twisting serpent - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:79: The fifth Heichal is the one called Sheol; corresponding to it, the evil inclination is called Arel [Uncircumcised], and it is the essence of the foreskin. In this Heichal there is one gate, and over it one appointed officer named Eivah [Enmity], and he arouses strife and enmities in the world; after his name this Heichal is called Eivah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:80: In this Heichal is one impure spirit who rules over everything, named Shodad [Despoiler], and he arouses plunder and destruction, and he crouches in the high mountains among rocks and cliffs. From this Heichal all those robbers nurse; and from here go forth all those murderers and killers who follow the flame of the whirling sword to kill everything. And when there is famine in the world, Heaven forfend, this spirit, called Shod [Plunder], pairs up with another named Kafan [Hunger] - this one to plunder the people of the world and kill them, and this is called Shod; and this one to curse the food in their bellies so that they will not be satisfied, and this is called Kafan. And when there are in Israel those who perform acts of loving-kindness in a time of famine, they cause these spirits not to rule in the world over Israel, and instead they rule over the idol-worshipping nations, and the side of impurity is subdued and Israel is blessed. But when, Heaven forfend, there is no one in Israel to perform loving-kindness, then, Heaven forfend, the husk grows strong, and one of these gives sustenance to the aforementioned nations and nurses all the flow of holiness - and of this it is said (Song of Songs 1:6), "they made me keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have not kept" - this is Israel, for all the flow descends from holiness to the other side, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:81: Under those we mentioned there are impure spirits called Orlah [Foreskin], and they are the "shoots of the foreskin" and the "branches of the foreskin," and over all of them there is one appointed officer named Gezardina, and he is appointed over all those who do not observe the two years of orlah [the prohibition on fruit of a tree's first three years], and all those who delay circumcision - and this is the reason for "the bridegroom of blood" of Zipporah - and he is appointed over a person when he defiles his covenant, to bring him into Sheol and Avaddon to be judged there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:82: In the middle of this Heichal there is one spirit who lies in wait on the roads and in places to see those who transgress the Torah, to inform on them above, to introduce enmity between the upper and lower [worlds]; and so too they all stand to entice a person from the good way to the evil way, and afterward ascend and accuse him, and end up bringing him out from this world and from the World to Come - and there is no greater enmity than this, and therefore it is called Heichal Eivah. And this spirit is named Afra, meaning "ash/dust" that produces no fruit and grows no plants, the opposite of holy ash which produces fruit; the reason being, as already explained, that every spirit of impurity is castrated. And this is the ash of the burnt sin-offering, for it is bound to sin, which is the twisting serpent; and further, when a person sins, this dust grows strong through the serpent - and this is included in the bitter waters that bring the curse; and this is the dust of the Tabernacle floor that the priest would give the sotah [suspected adulteress] to drink, because she went astray and turned after the seducing serpent - he gives her to drink from the dust of the floor of the Tabernacle, which is this dust in the bitter water, and this spirit rules over her and consumes her - and these are the [spiritually] guilty "last waters" [an allusion to the halachic practice of washing after a meal] - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:83: The sixth Heichal - this Heichal is uppermost over all the Heichalot, like the side of holiness, for "this corresponding to that God has made," as I explained. In this Heichal there are four gates, and in them four impure companies, called: one Mavet [Death], one Ra [Evil], one Tzalmavet [Shadow of Death], and one Ofel [Gloom]. These stand forever to do evil and to accuse, and the four of them unite as one, like the side of holiness; and because of this aforementioned union, it is called "Beit Chaver" [House of Companionship/Union], as it is written (Proverbs 21:9), "than with a quarrelsome wife and a house of company [chaver]" - and this is "and a binder of spells [chover chaver]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:84: Of this Heichal it is said (ibid. 27:6), "profuse are the kisses of an enemy [sonei]" - here stand all those kisses and enticements and bodily lusts of harlotry and adultery, through which a person is banished from this world and from the World to Come; all those written of in Proverbs (ibid. 7:6), in the passage "for at the window of my house, through my lattice," and so on - all those enticements are from the side of the spirit of this Heichal.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:85: And of her it is said (ibid. 7:11), "her feet do not stay at home" - for she goes to entice people; after she has enticed him, she gives him to taste the cruel venom of vipers and takes out his soul with her sword, and in it are three drops: with one, his soul is thrown into confusion and finds no place to rest; with the second, his soul is uprooted and departs; with the third, his face turns green and his soul departs like a bursting bubble, and so on - all this to the one drawn after her; and this is what Scripture says (ibid. 5:4), "but her end is bitter as wormwood," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:86: In this Heichal stand all those accusers who entice a person through his garments and clothes, that he curl his body and fuss with his hair and wash his body and beautify his appearance so that women will gaze at him; and over this matter there is one appointed officer named Sektofa. Within [the domain of] this officer stands another officer named Mareh [Mirror/Appearance], through whom a person looks at himself and beautifies himself and curls himself and looks in that mirror and clothes himself in pride and arrogance and haughtiness of spirit. And then another power in the Heichal, named Asirta, who is appointed over all dreams, to show a person an image that he will be drawn after, to destroy his soul; and this officer arouses another officer under his hand, who descends and arouses in the lower Heichal, in which is Askarah, and there he arouses one female, who is Lilith, mother of demons; and when a person is aroused in his haughtiness [through] the officer Asirta, then Lilith binds herself with him, and then, every single New Moon, the "mirror" we mentioned is aroused, together with Lilith; and sometimes a person is harmed by them and falls to the ground and is seized [epileptically] and harmed - and all this the "mirror" caused him, and according to the extent of his pride, so is the extent of his evil and harm and impurity; and this is (Proverbs 7:23), "till an arrow pierces his liver," and so on - may the Merciful One save us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:87: The seventh Heichal - this Heichal is the Heichal of the dregs of wine, to become drunk from it, as it is written (Genesis 9:21), "and he became drunk and uncovered himself within his tent" - and these are the grapes that Eve pressed, through which she caused death to her husband and to all who came after him: (Deuteronomy 32:32), "their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:88: In this Heichal stand all those impure souls to give sustenance to all those who defile themselves with a menstruating woman, or a married woman, and the like of them - such as mamzerim [children of forbidden unions]; and he is called mamzer because he is from a foreign god [El zar]. And according to the nature of the transgression and the matter of the evil inclination, so is the soul drawn upon him from this Heichal, and all who see them recognize them, that they are disqualified seed, a mamzer from a foreign god, and all his deeds testify against him that he is disqualified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:89: From this Heichal goes forth one spirit who is appointed over all these souls, named Tzefoni [Northern One]; and your mnemonic is (Joel 2:20), "and I will remove the northern one [tzefoni] far from you." Corresponding to this Heichal in Gehinnom is called Eretz Tachtit. In this Heichal is a fine point close to the sefirot of the husks, and from it emerge all those fine spirits that roam the world, which see but are not seen; and these stand to perform wonders for people, for they do not stand in filthy husks as much as the others.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:90: Over these there is one appointed officer named Nesira, and this is an Aramaic word meaning "cut off," meaning that he is separated from the most impure husks; and these fly in the air and cause harm on their impure side, to perform wonders in the world for those who stand on the side of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:91: From this Heichal go forth strong fire, and snow, and a mighty wind, to judge the wicked; and this is what Scripture says (Psalms 68:15), "it snows on Tzalmon."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:92: In this Heichal stand four gates, open to the four directions; and these grasp and do not grasp on the side of holiness, and there the light of holiness shines, and it is a place prepared for the pious ones of the nations of the world who did not do evil to Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:93: At the gate of the middle Heichal, outside, there are 300 gates, and they correspond to holiness; and they are places for the pious kings of the nations of the world who did not do evil to Israel and did not oppress them and shielded them - and they have honor there for this, and the light of holiness shines for them within that gloom; and of this it is said (Isaiah 14:18), "all the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in glory, each in his own house."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:94: But if they oppressed Israel, several angels of destruction seize them and judge them three times every day with several strange judgments; every single day they testify against Israel and against their faith.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:95: Up to here the matter of these Heichalot is concluded. Indeed, I copied this from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Parashat Pekudei), and at first glance it would seem that these are Heichalot corresponding to the sefirah of the husks that we mentioned in the previous Gate; however, it appears that the sefirot are included within the Heichalot, and the Heichalot and the husks are all one matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:96: And corresponding to these seven are seven kinds of evil inclination, which receives its power from these seven; therefore the evil inclination is called by seven names, and these are: Ra [Evil], Tamei [Impure], Sonei [Enemy], Even [Stone], Michshol [Stumbling-block], Arel [Uncircumcised], Tzefoni [Northern]. And corresponding to these are seven compartments in Gehinnom in which the sinner is judged according to these seven kinds, and these are: Bor, Shachat, Dumah, Tit HaYaven, Sheol, Tzalmavet, Eretz Tachtit - and they correspond to each other: purity against impurity, fitness against disqualification, permitted against forbidden, merit against guilt - for "this too, corresponding to that, God has made," as I explained in the previous chapters - to this point, the words of my teacher, peace be upon him, in the book Pardes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:97: Further, one must fear the belief in reincarnation (gilgul) - which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, taught us, and Pythagoras agreed with them, though many disagree with this view - for it is very bitter for the soul, more bitter than the judgment of Gehinnom. And my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote that it is comparable to a man who went on a trading journey of two or three years to a certain place, thinking he would profit from that merchandise there; upon arriving there, they told him: all your labor was for nothing and in vain, for this merchandise in your hand is worth nothing in this place - and that poor man returned dejected. How much distress comes to this man over his lack of wisdom and understanding, that he did not investigate and inquire what merchandise was suitable for that place, by which he could profit - and the parable is understood by itself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:98: And especially when a person knows that most of the souls in our generation are reincarnated, and have come now to fix what they did not fix originally - for if he departs from the world without fixing what he came for, then all his toil and labor in this world is found to be in vain, and he must return a third and a fourth time until he is fixed, and his punishment is great for not having fixed it the first time.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:99: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote (Pinchas 213a), in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, this person who takes on the reincarnation of a soul and does not merit to be fixed through it is as though he lies to the truth of the King, and I apply to him this verse (Leviticus 5:22 [6:3]), "or has found a lost item and denies it, and swears falsely" - "and denies it" - better for him had he not been created - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:100: And especially if his reincarnated soul was the soul of some wicked person, so that he is found building on a shaky foundation, and he must first fix the foundation and only afterward build upon it, as is explained there further on; and the fix is through repentance and accepting sufferings upon himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:101: And concerning why a soul would need reincarnation after it has been purified in Gehinnom, my teacher, peace be upon him, answered that reincarnation is for two reasons: the first, for a deficiency in a commandment that was not completed, and it must return and complete it properly, and for this it is forced to reincarnate - for Gehinnom is only for purification alone, but not to complete a deficiency.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:102: And further, it is possible that it comes to fix and purify what Gehinnom cannot purify - for there are sins that Gehinnom purifies and there are sins that Gehinnom does not purify, and it is forced to come to complete [the fix]. The parable for this is a person afflicted with plagues in his body and limbs: there are plagues that a doctor can heal without cutting off an entire limb, but rather cuts a little of that rotten flesh until he heals; and sometimes it happens that the entire limb must be cut off so that he not die and the plague reach his heart - then he cuts off the whole limb, and that person is found blemished, missing one limb, one arm or one leg and the like. And in this manner, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not desire that a person who blemished one limb so severely that, were he to enter Gehinnom, that whole limb would be entirely nullified and he would remain blemished in the Garden of Eden - rather, he returns to the world to be fixed, and then he may be blemished according to the limb with which he originally sinned, and then he must, at his death, do repentance, and thereby fix what happened in the previous incarnation. However, Gehinnom is only to purify sins whose purification does not involve severing a limb - and this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Eruvin 19a): the fire of Gehinnom has no power over the transgressors of Israel, by a kal vachomer [a fortiori] from the golden altar - and this is the matter of the rule that it would rule over them entirely to consume them, but rather it purifies from outside that darkness and blemish that is in the limbs of the soul, and it is like the parable of a doctor who places a medicine on the wound to eat away that bad flesh; and when the soul leaves Gehinnom it is missing from the flesh of its limbs, as in the parable we made, and its deficiency is completed through the light of the sun of righteousness and healing in its wings, mentioned above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:103: And concerning the matter of the judgment of reincarnation, the Sava explains in Parashat Mishpatim (Zohar 99b), and we will copy a little of his words to arouse the heart; in these words: "if he takes another for himself" (Exodus 21:10) - the reincarnations alluded to in this verse are how great and lofty they are! For all souls enter into reincarnation, and people do not know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and how the scale stands, and how people are judged every day and every moment, and how souls enter into judgment before they come into this world, and how they enter into judgment after they leave this world - how many reincarnations and how many hidden deeds the Holy One, blessed be He, performs with naked souls, and how many naked spirits go about in that world that do not enter within the King's curtain, and how many worlds are overturned through them, and the world that is overturned in several hidden wonders - and people do not know and do not take heed, and how souls are hurled about like a stone in a sling, as it is said (I Samuel 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies, He will sling out as from the hollow of a sling" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:104: And you must know that the secret of reincarnation depends on the secret of thought, as it is written (II Samuel 14:14), "and he devises means, that His banished one not remain banished from him." And there is further proof from the Tikkunim (100a), which says there, "and with a yud, reincarnation is effected"; see there. Therefore one must fear reincarnation, for that is the place of fear, as I explained in chapter 2, and it is a place where the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous to a hair's breadth - for it says in the Tikkunim (132a), which we copied in chapter 9, that every limb that was not properly fixed comes back in reincarnation - even a voice or an utterance that was not brought forth with awe and love, so that the Name be complete, comes back in reincarnation. Therefore let every man tremble greatly over this, and be exacting in his deeds, and complete his soul properly, so as not to burden his Maker.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:105: Further, concerning the matter of the purification of the soul in the River of Fire, it is explained in the Tikkunim (there, 4a), in these words: (Ezekiel 1:1), "and I was among the exiles by the river Chebar" - this is the River of Fire, which is drawn forth and emerges from before Him; "a thousand thousands ministered to Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand angels stood before Him," and so on (Daniel 7:10) - and souls are immersed in this River of Fire, from the filth with which they were soiled in the lowly world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:106: And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, concerning this matter, the reason why souls, after being purified in Gehinnom, need to immerse in the River of Fire; and he said that there are two kinds of purification for the soul: the first, in the Gehinnom that is in the earth, which is to purify for what it blemished by heating itself in the fire of the inclination to transgress the commandments; and the second is to purify for what it did not sanctify itself in what was permitted to it, along the lines of what they said, "sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you" - such as the matter of excessive eating and the other matters that will be explained in the matter of holiness, with God's help. And these matters are not a complete blemish to the soul, for there is no [true] blemish except from the side of a negative commandment; but this is the filth of this world and its desires, for this world and its desires are clothed in the serpent's skin, and when a person does not separate from it, that filth remains acquired in his soul; and Gehinnom purifies only with physical fire a physical blemish - namely, the fire of the inclination, which is a great blemish - but this, which is not a [true] blemish, requires a fine and spiritual fire: the upper River of Fire, drawn from the Throne of Glory, of which it is written (Daniel 7:9), "its throne was fiery flames" - and through it, all the physicality of this world is stripped away.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:107: And there is proof of this from Rashbi (Vayakhel 211b), in these words: and these four river-heads that reach the holy Throne, and from their sweat they sweat, and from that sweat of their sweating that River of Fire is made, as it is written (Daniel 7:10), "a river of fire flowed and came forth from before Him; a thousand thousands ministered to Him." And souls, when they ascend, are washed in that River of Fire and ascend as an offering, and are not burned but washed. Come and see, from the salamander from which they make a garment: and since it is from fire, that garment is washed only in fire - the fire consumes the filth that is in it and that garment is washed. So too the soul of fire, which is taken from within the holy Throne, of which it is written, "its throne was fiery flames" - at the time it needs to be washed from that filth upon it, it is brought into the fire and is washed, and the fire consumes all that filth that is in the soul, and the soul is washed and refined.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:108: And should you say, if so, then there is no punishment at all for the soul in this. Come and see: woe to the soul that bears a foreign fire! Even though it is refined, when the filth upon it is great, woe to the soul that bears that punishment - because that filth is refined by fire twice. The first time: once it received its punishment in the body, the soul goes and they take it and bring it into a certain place called Ben Hinnom. And why is it called Ben Hinnom? Rather, there is one place in Gehinnom where souls are refined by refining, to be purified, before they enter the Garden of Eden; and if those souls are righteous, when they bring them into that place, two angels are ready in the Garden of Eden and stand at the gate and call out to those officers who are in that place of Gehinnom, in order to receive that soul. And that soul, before it has been refined by fire, those officers call out to them [the waiting angels] and say, "hinam" [they are not yet ready/here]; and at times when it has been refined and those officers go out with it from that place and prepare it to go to the gate of the Garden of Eden where those agents are, they say to them, "hinam" [behold, here they are] - these are the souls that have now been refined. Then that soul enters the Garden of Eden, and how broken it is from that breaking of the refining of Gehinnom - which is the breaking of the lower fire that descends from above; but once it reaches the lower earth, it is a fire that is not fine, and the soul is punished by it and broken. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, brings forth the sun that shines from those four gates of rivers in the firmament that is over the Garden [of Eden], and it reaches that soul and heals it - this is (Malachi 3:20), "but for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:109: The second time: afterward, when it sits in the lower Garden of Eden - all that time it sits, and until now it has not separated entirely from those matters of the visions of this world - when they bring it up above, it must separate from every vision and from every matter of the lower [world], and they bring it through that River of Fire; then the soul is entirely refined through it, and goes out and appears before the Master of the world, purified on every side. Once it gazes into that light, it is healed and completed from everything; and then those souls stand in garments, crowned before their Master. Happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:110: Behold, our intent in this passage is explained explicitly, in that it says, "when they bring it up above, it must separate from every vision and from every matter of the lower [world]." And incidentally it is explained how much distress reaches the soul under the rule of the fire of the lower Gehinnom, because it is physical relative to the fineness of the soul, and it is broken until the light of the supernal sun from the World of Atzilut comes. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that it shines from the side of Arich Anpin, in whom is all lengthening [patience] and healing, and therefore it has the power to heal every wound that may be in the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:111: Further, one must fear the Day of Judgment, for even Samuel was afraid of it, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 4b): "and Samuel said to Saul, why have you disturbed me, to bring me up?" (I Samuel 28:15) - Rabbi Elazar, when he would reach this verse, would weep: and if Samuel the prophet was afraid of the Day of Judgment, how much more so are we! What is [the source for] this? As it is written (I Samuel 28:13), "and the woman said to Saul, I saw a god-like being coming up out of the earth" - "coming up" implies two: one, Samuel; and the other, that Samuel went and brought Moses with him. He said: perhaps, Heaven forbid, I am being summoned to judgment - come up with me, in case there is something written in the Torah that I did not fulfill - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:112: Further, they said in the Midrash, Bereshit Rabbah (93:10): Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said, woe to us from the Day of Judgment, woe to us from the day of rebuke! Balaam, the wise man of the nations, could not withstand the rebuke of his donkey, as it is said (Numbers 22:30), "have I ever been accustomed to do so to you? And he said, no." Joseph was the youngest of the tribes, and his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed before him - when the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to rebuke each and every one according to his deeds, how much more so! As it is said (Psalms 50:21), "I will rebuke you and set it in order before your eyes."
